pitch: The practical guide to drawing the current value stream, imagining the future state and charting the path to get there.
br: matrix · shared steps · one at a time
one piece at a time · cells · combine
office · too much detail · no follow-up
quiz: What does a value stream map cover?
One product family, door to door
You follow the path of a group of products that go through similar steps.
Where do you start collecting the flow on the floor?
At shipping, closest to the customer
You walk the flow from downstream to upstream, starting from the customer.
What is the map's main contribution compared with classic process maps?
It connects material flow and information flow
In a lean plant, it is information that tells each step what to produce and when.
What does the timeline at the bottom of the map show?
The gap between total lead time and actual processing time
A few minutes of real work amid weeks of waiting.
What main problem do most current-state maps reveal?
Overproduction: each step produces according to its own schedule
Inventory between steps is its visible symptom.
What should you do where continuous flow isn't possible?
A controlled inventory from which downstream takes and which upstream replenishes.
The only process that receives the customer schedule
The other steps are connected to it by continuous flow or supermarkets.
Releasing work in small, regular increments so delays show up in minutes
A multiple of takt, often one container: you know very quickly if you are ahead or behind.
